report.source_text: Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging revealed a large heterogeneous mass extending from the right pulmonary hilum through the diaphragm (Fig. 1). The lesion involved segments VII and VIII of the liver. There was a small pleural effusion and no evidence of distant metastases. The mass appeared to be distinct from the pericardium and there was no pleural effusion (Fig. 2).

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old female presented with generalized fatigue, fever, night sweats, cough, and pleuritic chest pain. Initial laboratory findings showed leukocytosis, and a viral panel was negative for common respiratory viruses. Imaging (CT and MRI) revealed a large heterogeneous mass extending from the right pulmonary hilum through the diaphragm, involving liver segments VII and VIII, with a small pleural effusion and no distant metastases. A biopsy of this mass confirmed pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma, characterized by high-grade malignant spindle cell proliferation and positive immunostains for low molecular weight cytokeratin Cam 5.2. A subsequent PET scan showed no additional disease. Surgical consultation led to deferral of surgery due to transdiaphragmatic invasion. The patient was started on systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and was tolerating treatment without complication at a 3-week follow-up.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with generalized fatigue, fever, night sweats, cough, and pleuritic chest pain.
Initial laboratory findings included leukocytosis of 13.5 white blood cells per microliter and negative viral panel for respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and COVID-19.

Initial imaging (CT and MRI) revealed a large heterogeneous mass extending from the right pulmonary hilum through the diaphragm, involving segments VII and VIII of the liver, with a small pleural effusion and no distant metastases.

Biopsy confirmed pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma, characterized by a high-grade, malignant spindle cell proliferation with occasional multinucleated giant cells, inter-lesional acute and chronic inflammation, and diffuse positivity for low molecular weight cytokeratin Cam 5.2 on immunostains.
Positron-emission tomography revealed no additional disease.
Surgery was deferred due to transdiaphragmatic invasion after surgical consult.
Patient was tolerating treatment without complication at 3-week follow-up.
